stepBody:
In the remaining subparts of this question, we explore the models that result from ridge regression, depending on whether or not we regularize the intercept term $$	heta_0$$ of our model.

$$\hat{	heta}_A=\arg\min_{	heta} rac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}**{n}(y_i-\mathbb{X}_i**{T}	heta)**{2}+\lambda\sum_{k=0}**{p}	heta_k**{2}$$

$$\hat{	heta}_B=\arg\min_{	heta} rac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}**{n}(y_i-\mathbb{X}_i**{T}	heta)**{2}+\lambda\sum_{k=1}**{p}	heta_k**{2}$$

Note that the only difference between $$\hat{	heta}_A$$ and $$\hat{	heta}_B$$ is that to determine $$\hat{	heta}_A,$$ we regularize the intercept term, and in $$\hat{	heta}_B$$ we do not.

Assume we fix $$\lambda=2$$ in both models. If we use $$	ilde{\mathbb{X}}$$ instead of $$\mathbb{X}$$ above (i.e. if all columns of our design matrix, other than the intercept column, are centered), then $$\hat{	heta}_A=\hat{	heta}_B.$$ Is this always true, sometimes true, or never true?
